expression_restriction.value: Full-face shot, applicant facing the camera directly; side or angled views are not accepted

expression.en: Photographs must be full-face shots with the applicant facing the camera directly; side or angled views are not accepted.
expression.ko: 사진은 얼굴 정면을 촬영해야 하며 신청자가 카메라를 직접 응시해야 한다. 측면이나 각도가 있는 사진은 허용되지 않는다.
expression.ja: 写真は正面から撮影し、申請者はカメラを直接見つめなければならない。側面や斜めからの写真は認められない。

db_conflicts.research_value: 2 x 2 inch (5.08 x 5.08cm), per the Embassy of the State of Libya in Washington, D.C., applied consistently across all listed visa types (diplomatic, business, spouse, journalist, Libyan citizens holding foreign passports, and tourist visas)

cross_verification.note_en: The Embassy of the State of Libya in Washington, D.C. (embassyoflibyadc.org/visa, an official Libyan diplomatic mission) was directly fetched and states: 'One recent passport-size (2x2 inch) color photograph with a white background' and 'Photographs must be full-face shots in which the applicant is facing the camera directly (Side or angle views are NOT accepted)', explicitly repeated across every visa category on that page. This 2x2 inch (5.08cm x 5.08cm) figure is notably different from the DB's '4 x 6cm' -- flagged as a db_conflict. This is a US-style photo dimension (identical to the common American visa-photo convention), distinct from the 4x6cm figure that appears to apply to Libya's domestic passport photo convention -- it is plausible the two differ by design (embassy/consular visa photos historically following a US-influenced 2x2in convention while the passport itself follows a different national/ECOWAS-style convention), but this could not be independently cross-confirmed against a Libyan-government-run (as opposed to embassy-run) visa portal, since evisa.gov.ly's pages returned no substantive text content (only a bare 'E-visa' heading) on every fetch attempt in this research pass.
